messages:
customer-support: FYI — Customer ACME reported big p95 jump on /v1/generate after the runtime rollout in us-west-2 canary. They see p95 ~1.6s vs baseline ~600ms. Escalated to SEV. request ids: rq_8a2f, rq_8a31, rq_8a45
ana: on it. timeframe? can you paste the sample req ids and any warm/cold indicator? :eyes:
customer-support: Happened around 2024-11-02T14:03Z. Attached 10 sample request ids and a short trace. They say responses look slower after model kvcache hits. No increase in errors, just latency.
rico: thanks — I'm looking at canary rollout logs now. linking grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood/inference/p95?env=canary&region=us-west-2
meera: I see the same p95 spike for canary hosts that got runtime v2.14. Request rate steady, cpu/gpu utilization normal. Queueing looks up on some hot-paths.
jamal: logs from one request: ```
[2024-11-02T14:03:12Z] rq_8a2f start total_ms=42
[2024-11-02T14:03:12Z] rq_8a2f runtime_enqueue_ms=8
[2024-11-02T14:03:13Z] rq_8a2f runtime_dequeue_ms=982
[2024-11-02T14:03:13Z] rq_8a2f model_kv_hit=true seq_len=128
[2024-11-02T14:03:13Z] rq_8a2f finish total_ms=1038
```
meera: dequeue_ms ~982ms — that's the hot path. looks like batch scheduling delay.
ana: any recent scheduler changes in v2.14? I remember a scheduler rewrite landed last week.
rico: yes, v2.14 introduced the 'adaptive-batch-slew' kernel scheduler and changed the batch timeout heuristic from 8ms -> 12ms for some backends. Could be interacting with small burst traffic.
meera: hypothesis: longer batch timeout increases max wait for small bursts and pushes p95 up even if throughput is fine.
ana: can we reproduce locally with the canary image? steps to repro please.
customer-support: customer provided a synthetic profile: 20rps 50% short prompts (<=32 tokens), 50% medium (<=256).
jamal: I'm spinning up a canary agent with v2.14 and running the profile now. quick check: `curl -X POST https://canary-agent/v1/replay -d @profile.json`
sre-bot: alert: canary-hosts-uw2-v2.14 registered increased queueing metric at 2024-11-02T14:02Z. p95 deviation +170% relative to baseline.
rico: local repro confirms — with default scheduler timeout we see p95 ~1.5s for short prompts. if i force timeout back to 8ms the p95 drops to ~620ms.
ana: good repro. options: 1) rollback scheduler change in canary, 2) tweak timeout to 8ms as a quick mitigation, 3) add routing rule to steer short prompt traffic away from canary while we investigate.
meera: adding temporary routing rule is lowest risk. We can update smart routing to prefer stable cluster for tenants with p95 SLA until fix.
jamal: I'll prepare a hotfix patch to expose `scheduler.timeout_ms` as an operator flag (default 12ms) so we can flip to 8ms without full rollback. PR draft: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/1482
ana: QA: need a quick canary test after flag flip. Also add a perf test that ramps short-prompt traffic.
customer-support: customer asked for ETA and whether we can route their traffic off canary now. They want a temporary mitigation ASAP.
ana: action items: @jamal flip scheduler timeout flag on canary to 8ms (hotfix) and post results, @rico prepare routing rule to exclude ACME from canary and fallback to stable, @meera run perf test and attach p95 numbers. I'll coordinate with CS for customer comms.
jamal: hotfix applied to canary (timeout=8ms) — retesting now.
jamal: retest results: p95 reduced to 610ms for the profile. logs snippet: ```
[2024-11-02T14:15:02Z] rq_9b5c runtime_dequeue_ms=27
[2024-11-02T14:15:02Z] rq_9b5c finish total_ms=598
```
rico: routing rule ready; staging push done. Once approved I'll promote to prod to steer ACME.
meera: perf test doc: short-profile -> p95: baseline 600ms, canary-12ms 1500ms, canary-8ms 620ms. attaching graph (uploaded).
ana: good. next: we should bisect whether the scheduler rewrite or kernel selector interactions amplify the effect. @jamal can you run a bisect between commits that introduced adaptive batching vs kernel selector tweak? keep canary image but toggle features.
jamal: running bisect now — will toggle adaptive-batch flag and kernel-selector flag independently. timeline ~2-3 hours.
customer-support: thanks team — pls keep me posted and we'll notify ACME about the mitigation routing. :thumbsup:
ana: thanks everyone. keep this thread for final RCA and follow-up perf test cases to prevent regression in future rollouts.
